Part 3. The new design, from the top down

Cycle 1. The whole in one picture

Version 2 runs left to right in four stages (Figure 5). Files hold the generators (one file per drawable object or script) and your saved work. A document records what you made: which generators, with which settings, where, and which points they share. The document is turned into geometry: paths, stitch lines and named points, all as plain data. Geometry becomes output: the screen, a thumbnail, or a printed template.

You change the document and nothing else, by commands: drag, slide, weld, undo. Under the geometry stage sits the kernel, the small vocabulary every drawing is written in. Part 4 is about that vocabulary.

[[FIG cycle1 | Cycle 1: files, document, geometry, output]]

Three things are kept strictly apart. The kernel is geometry only: values in, values out, no canvas and no memory. Generators describe objects and hold no state. Documents are plain data and hold no code. Most of Part 2's weaknesses come from these three being mixed.

Cycle 2. The blocks

Figure 6 opens up the four stages into the blocks that do the work. Arrows show which block uses which; none points upward.

[[FIG cycle2 | Cycle 2: the blocks]]

What you touch. The screens are the six tabs you know. Interaction is the one place mouse and keys are understood: it works out what is under the cursor and turns a gesture into a command. Controls builds sliders and boxes from an object's settings. The commands table holds every menu item and button in one list. The library view is today's category list builder, kept as it is.

What keeps track. Commands and history is the only way the document changes; it keeps a copy of the document before each change, which is what makes undo work. Session holds what you are looking at (selection, mode, zoom), which is never saved and never undone. The document is what you made.

The drawing model (shaded). The evaluator turns the document into geometry, layer by layer, using the generators and the kernel. The renderers are the only code that paints: screen, thumbnail, SVG, PDF.

Files and scripts. The script host runs each script in its own sealed room, so nothing carries over. Catalog and storage is the only door to files: the lists you see are worked out from the folders, so there is nothing to rebuild or keep in step. The Node service does the writing and watches the folders.

Cycle 3. Three actions, followed through the blocks

Dragging a handle. Figure 7 follows one drag on a Parabola layer whose corner another layer is attached to. Look at step 4: the drag changes one entry in the point table, and nothing else. Everything after that is recomputed from the document, which is why nothing can be left out of step.

[[FIG walk_drag | Dragging a handle, block by block]]

Adding a script. You save a file into a library folder. The Node service notices, reads the file's description without running it, and tells the open program, which adds the item to its list (Figure 8). Edit the file in VS Code and save again, and an open drawing reruns with your settings kept.

[[FIG dynamic_add | Adding a script by saving a file]]

Undo. Before each command, the whole document is copied onto the history (Figure 9). Undo puts the previous copy back; redo moves forward again. "Unsaved changes" just means you are not at the position where you last saved. Undo back to it, and the figure is clean again.

[[FIG undo_stack | The history: one copy of the document per step]]
